name: New Order
label: Factory Records
lede: Three survivors of Joy Division learned to sing, play synths and program drum machines in public, then made the best-selling 12-inch single ever and spent the money on a nightclub. Thirty years later they were in court over the name.

eras.title: Somebody has to sing
eras.text: Two months after Ian Curtis died, the rest of Joy Division were back on a stage with no name and no singer. Nobody wanted the job, so Bernard Sumner took it, and Rob Gretton found a name in a newspaper.

years.h: An unnamed trio plays the Beach Club, Manchester
years.p: Sumner, [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]] and [[Stephen Morris|b3036249-8b39-4d02-a312-d31a63497bbc]] debut ten weeks after Curtis's death. They had already tried demos with singer Kevin Hewick, at [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]]'s suggestion.

years.h: Gretton finds the name in a Guardian headline
years.p: "The New Order of Kampuchean Rebels" gives the band its name. The Witch Doctors of Zimbabwe was also on the list.
years.xp: The band said the name wasn't meant to refer to Nazism or fascism. After Joy Division's name and the An Ideal for Living sleeve, the accusation came anyway, and the band spent years answering it.

years.cap: New Order with Gillian Gilbert, Hal 4, Rotterdam, December 13, 1980
years.h: Gillian Gilbert's first gig, at the Squat in Manchester
years.p: Gretton suggested [[Gillian Gilbert|c970c5cd-facf-4c49-babf-a5b688c1ec40]], Morris's girlfriend, for keyboards and guitar. It frees Sumner, who struggled to sing and play guitar at once.

years.h: 'Ceremony', FAC 33, with Sumner singing words he had to decode
years.p: Joy Division played it live once, at their last gig. Curtis never wrote the words down, so Sumner ran the rehearsal tape through a graphic equaliser to hear them.
years.xp:
Sumner said Joy Division wrote it "to try and heal him through music." New Order cut it with [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]]; Hook said the best thing to come out of it was Hannett showing them how to use a mixing desk.

A second version with Gilbert came out as a 12-inch that September. The single reached No. 34 and topped the indie chart.

years.h: Movement leaves Strawberry Studios half-loved
years.p: Hook sings 'Dreams Never End' and 'Doubts Even Here'. The band said in 1982 they were happy with the songs, not all happy with the production.
years.xp:
Saville's sleeve borrowed from a Fortunato Depero futurist poster; the lines spell an F for Factory and an L, Roman 50, for FACT 50.

Years later Hook came round: "I think Movement gets a raw deal in general, really."

years.h: Hannett walks out in the middle of 'Everything's Gone Green'
years.p: So the band produces the next single, 'Temptation', itself. Trips to New York had them listening to electro, post-disco and Italian disco, and Morris was teaching himself drum programming.

eras.title: A club, a floppy disk, a famous loss
eras.text: Factory's own nightclub opened on New Order money, and the band made a single that sounded like nothing else on British radio. Both became legends. Only one of them made money.

years.cap: The Haçienda on its opening night, May 1982
years.src: Wikipedia: The Haçienda · Wikipedia: New Order
years.h: The Haçienda opens as FAC 51, and Bernard Manning gives his fee back
years.p: Ben Kelly designs the interior at 11–13 Whitworth Street West. Opening-night comic Bernard Manning dies on stage and returns the money.
years.xp:
Manning's review of the room: "I've played some shit-holes during my time, but this is really something."

The club was largely funded by New Order and lost money for years before acid house filled it.

years.cap: FAC 73, the die-cut floppy disk sleeve
years.src: Wikipedia: Blue Monday · Wikipedia: New Order
years.h: 'Blue Monday' comes out in a sleeve that costs more than it earns
years.p: Sumner built the sequencer, Morris programmed an Oberheim DMX, and the choir is sampled off Kraftwerk. It goes on to be the best-selling 12-inch single of all time.
years.xp:
Saville and Brett Wickens' die-cut sleeve, made to look like a floppy disk, cost so much that Factory lost money on copies. Wilson put it at 5p a sleeve; Saville has grumbled about the story ever since.

Sumner named Klein + M.B.O.'s 'Dirty Talk' and Sylvester's 'You Make Me Feel (Mighty Real)' as starting points. Hook said it was "stolen" from Donna Summer's 'Our Love'.

yt: 'Blue Monday' on Top of the Pops, 1983
years.h: New Order insist on playing 'Blue Monday' live on Top of the Pops
years.p: No miming on the BBC. Morris remembers the synthesisers going awry; the single peaks at No. 9 anyway.

years.h: Fantin-Latour's roses on a dance record
years.p: Self-produced at Britannia Row, FACT 75 reaches No. 4. Saville put Henri Fantin-Latour's A Basket of Roses from the National Gallery on the front and a colour-code alphabet on the back.
years.xp: Saville went to the gallery looking for a Renaissance portrait. The flowers, he said, were seductive, the way power, corruption and lies are.

years.cap: New Order on stage at the SFX, Dublin, October 1983
years.h: Arthur Baker produces 'Confusion'
years.p: Made with the electro producer [[Arthur Baker|6b6c5ce7-7a49-463a-ac9f-ba97c953a77e]], the single wins best single at the NME Awards and lands the band in the clubs for good.

years.h: Madonna plays her first UK show at the Haçienda
years.p: Channel 4's The Tube broadcasts it from the club. The Haçienda was still losing money.

eras.title: Hollywood calls, MTV answers
eras.text: Every New Order album split the band down the middle, guitars on one side and machines on the other, Then the singles compilation went American.

years.h: Low-Life, and a Jonathan Demme video for 'The Perfect Kiss'
years.p: Guitars and sequencers on the same record. The video is directed by [[Jonathan Demme|d5563742-bec6-4f58-8db6-3ba276a5e3fa]].

years.h: Headlining G-Mex for the Festival of the Tenth Summer
years.p: Manchester marks ten years since the Pistols with New Order on top of a bill with [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]], [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] and [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]].

years.h: Brotherhood splits guitars and machines, side by side
years.p: Side one is guitars, side two is electronics. 'Bizarre Love Triangle' goes Top 20 in Australia and New Zealand.

years.h: 'True Faith' is New Order's first US Top 40 hit
years.p: The new single sells Substance, which gathers the 12-inches onto CD for the first time. The surreal video gets heavy MTV rotation and wins best British video at the 1988 Brits.

yt: 'Touched by the Hand of God' video
years.h: Kathryn Bigelow films 'Touched by the Hand of God' as hair metal
years.p: The band dress up as a glam-metal group. The single reaches No. 20 and No. 1 on the indie chart.

years.h: Quincy Jones's label remixes 'Blue Monday' to No. 3
years.p: 'Blue Monday 1988' climbs higher in the UK than the original did and tops the US dance chart.

years.h: Acid house fills the Haçienda
years.p: Fridays' Nude night and the new Hot night pack the club, which had lost money since 1982.

eras.title: Ibiza, Wembley and the receivers
eras.text: New Order recorded on a party island, took the England team to No. 1, and watched Factory sink with a club bleeding money. By 1993 Hook says he and Sumner hated each other.

years.h: Four months in Ibiza, and Technique was 20% done
years.p: Hook wanted out of dark London studios, so the band went to Mediterranean Sound. They finished at Peter Gabriel's Real World, and the album went straight to No. 1.
years.xp:
Morris on the island's DJs: "They'd put an acid record on and then the next one would be a Queen one." He added that the band were "a bit out of our brains."

Later, John Denver's publishers sued over 'Run 2', saying it echoed 'Leaving on a Jet Plane'. It was settled out of court and the song is now co-credited to Denver.

years.h: Monsters of Alternative Rock: touring the US with PiL and the Sugarcubes
years.p: New Order headline across North America with [[Public Image Ltd|68950696-ee9a-49b2-a8c2-d1d6c19355cc]], [[Throwing Muses|b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8]] and [[The Sugarcubes|95303251-46d5-4239-89c8-eaf0b0947a11]]. Side projects follow: Sumner's [[Electronic|3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d]] with [[Johnny Marr|ff621094-2a76-401f-8398-b75b5fd2be24]], Hook's [[Revenge|fa291018-ac66-454f-a42b-8fbcfb24d0b3]], and Morris and Gilbert's [[The Other Two|8a1fe33d-6029-462e-bcb7-08e0ebaba6dd]].

years.cap: New Order with the England squad for 'World in Motion', 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: World in Motion · Wikipedia: New Order
years.h: John Barnes raps, and New Order finally have a No. 1
years.p: 'World in Motion', the England World Cup song credited to EnglandNewOrder, is co-written with comic [[Keith Allen|74f549d5-6720-42d9-9977-8341ddda6059]]. It's the band's only UK No. 1.
years.xp:
The players cut their parts on March 25, 1990. Peter Beardsley, Paul Gascoigne, Steve McMahon and Des Walker all tried the rap first.

The working title was 'E for England'. The FA vetoed it once someone noticed what the E might stand for at the Haçienda.

years.src: Wikipedia: Factory Records · Wikipedia: New Order
years.h: Factory goes bankrupt, and New Order turn out to own their records
years.p: The band never signed a formal contract with Factory. Wilson said that was the main reason London Records' plan to buy the label fell through.

years.h: Republic tops the chart while the band falls apart
years.p: Hook's words for where he and Sumner were. Made with Stephen Hague to keep the Haçienda afloat, the first album on London Records hits No. 1 and gives the band its biggest US hit, 'Regret'.
years.xp:
While Sumner was away with Electronic, the others wrote a whole instrumental New Order album, which he shelved when he got back.

Band members had guaranteed loans that would have ruined them if Factory went under.

years.h: Reading Festival, then nothing for five years
years.p: After the Reading set, New Order go on hold. The members spend the break on Electronic, Revenge, Monaco and The Other Two.

eras.title: Clearing the air
eras.text: The Haçienda closed, Gretton called a meeting, and the band agreed to talk out their grudges before anyone played a note. It held for nine years.

years.h: The Haçienda closes for good
years.p: The last night was called Freak. Hook later said the club lost up to £18 million in its later years.
years.xp: Ecstasy took the place of beer, and bar money was the club's main income. Hook bought the name and wrote it up as The Haçienda: How Not to Run a Club in 2009. The building was knocked down in 2002 for flats.

years.h: Gretton gets the four back in a room
years.p: Before agreeing to any gig, they meet to iron out grudges. By the second meeting they're a band again, and they close Reading after Phoenix Festival is cancelled.
years.xp: Sumner: "We decided before we agreed to doing any gig, to have a meeting, and if anyone had any grudges to bear, to iron them out."

years.h: Get Ready goes back to guitars, with Billy Corgan on board
years.p: [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] plays and sings on 'Turn My Way'. [[Phil Cunningham|31408ce7-9f36-4c16-9b61-fe55c927e206]], formerly of [[Marion|52e90deb-1bcc-45c3-b2d3-9eed246cf063]], steps in live when Gilbert stays home to care for her and Morris's children.

years.h: Waiting for the Sirens' Call, with Cunningham as a full member
years.p: The same year, NME gives New Order and Joy Division its Godlike Genius award.

years.src: Wikipedia: Peter Hook · Wikipedia: New Order
years.h: Hook tells Xfm he and Sumner aren't working together
years.p: The band's own site answers that Hook can leave, but that doesn't end New Order. Sumner says in 2009 that he no longer wants to make music as New Order.

eras.title: New Order without Hook
eras.text: The band came back with Gilbert and without Hook, and Hook went to court. New Order kept touring and, after a decade, made a new album.

years.cap: New Order at the Fête de l'Humanité, near Paris
years.h: Back at the Ancienne Belgique, Brussels, with Gilbert and Tom Chapman
years.p: First shows since 2006: Brussels, then Paris's Bataclan the next night. [[Tom Chapman|8db4f238-3f18-4b08-aa69-d348fa630ce0]] of [[Bad Lieutenant|9726b890-6d3d-4118-8a12-6e000a14a005]] takes Hook's bass parts and Gilbert returns after ten years.

years.cap: New Order at the Tempodrom, Berlin, November 2015
years.h: Music Complete, the first album without Hook, on Mute
years.p: Signed to Mute Records in 2014, the band produces most of it themselves; Tom Rowlands of [[The Chemical Brothers|1946a82a-f927-40c2-8235-38d64f50d043]] does two tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: New Order · Wikipedia: Peter Hook
years.h: Hook sues Sumner, Morris and Gilbert over the New Order name
years.p: Court papers say the three had a company earning £7.8 million in four years while Hook got 1.25 per cent. They settled in September 2017.
years.xp: A judge found "at least a reasonable prospect" Hook could show he'd been treated unfairly. The September 2017 statement called it "a full and final settlement."

years.cap: New Order at the Manchester International Festival, July 2017
years.h: Liam Gillick builds New Order a stage in Manchester
years.p: The artist's collaboration with the band became the film New Order: Decades.

years.cap: New Order at the Royal Arena, Copenhagen
years.src: Wikipedia: New Order · Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
years.h: Morris and Gilbert step back from touring
years.p: The band announces the two won't tour for the foreseeable future. New Order and Joy Division also enter the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame this year, as one act.
